screening_decisions.reason: This study examines unpublished rating scales as a source of bias in schizophrenia trials. It is not an RCT testing benzodiazepines for TD treatment. Wrong topic entirely.
Systematic review comparing first vs second-generation antipsychotics for TD risk. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines. Wrong intervention (antipsychotics, not benzodiazepines).
Examines haloperidol serum concentrations and therapeutic response in schizophrenia. Not about benzodiazepines for TD treatment. Wrong intervention.
Animal study (Cebus apella monkeys) examining GABA levels in brains related to neuroleptic-induced dyskinesia. Not an RCT in humans, not testing benzodiazepines.

Tests diazepam (a benzodiazepine) in patients with tardive dyskinesia using a 24-week crossover design. Diazepam is administered to 13 subjects with TD. This appears to be a clinical trial testing a benzodiazepine for TD treatment. Meets population (TD patients), intervention (diazepam/benzodiazepine), and likely study design criteria. Conservative approach warrants inclusion for full-text review.
Review article updating TD rates in patients treated with first vs second-generation antipsychotics. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines. Wrong intervention.
Review paper on extrapyramidal symptoms with atypical antipsychotics. Discusses TD but does not test benzodiazepines. Wrong intervention.
Methodological paper linking BPRS scores to CGI ratings in schizophrenia trials. Not about benzodiazepines or TD treatment. Wrong topic.
Educational review about benzodiazepine teaching and clinical practice. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines for TD. Wrong study design and topic.
Review of incidence studies of TD associated with typical antipsychotics. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines. Wrong intervention.
Statistical methods note about cluster-randomized trials. Not about benzodiazepines or TD. Wrong topic.
Observational study examining predictors of TD improvement after neuroleptic discontinuation. Not an RCT, not testing benzodiazepines. Wrong study design and intervention.
Methodological paper comparing therapeutic efficacy indices. Not about benzodiazepines or TD treatment. Wrong topic.
Descriptive paper about the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale development. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines for TD. Wrong topic.
Review/discussion paper about atypical antipsychotics, drug-induced movement disorders, and discontinuation syndromes. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines for TD. Wrong intervention.
Review about benzodiazepine use, abuse, and dependence. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines for TD treatment. Wrong topic.
Cochrane review of NON-benzodiazepine GABA agonists (baclofen, progabide, sodium valproate, THIP) for TD. Selection criteria explicitly exclude benzodiazepines. Wrong intervention class.
Statistical methods paper about detecting skewness from summary data. Not about benzodiazepines or TD. Wrong topic.
General discussion paper about clinical research for schizophrenia treatment. Not an RCT testing benzodiazepines for TD. Wrong topic.
Cochrane review of calcium channel blockers (diltiazem, nifedipine, nimodipine, verapamil) for TD. Not testing benzodiazepines. Wrong intervention.
This study examines the clinical meaning of PANSS scores in schizophrenia drug trials. It does not address benzodiazepine treatment for tardive dyskinesia.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis comparing TD risk between first-generation and second-generation antipsychotics. It is not an RCT testing benzodiazepines for TD treatment.
This RCT compares haloperidol dosing regimens for acute schizophrenia. It does not address tardive dyskinesia or benzodiazepine treatment.

This controlled study compares two benzodiazepines (diazepam vs nitrazepam) for treating postneuroleptic tardive dyskinesia in 20 patients. Meets criteria as it compares benzodiazepines with another intervention in the target population.

This controlled study compares clonazepam (a benzodiazepine) versus phenobarbital (active placebo) in 21 psychiatric patients with tardive dyskinesia. Meets all criteria: controlled design, appropriate population, and benzodiazepine intervention.
This study reports effects of single IV/oral doses of various agents including diazepam on TD. It is a single-dose challenge study rather than a sustained treatment RCT.
This is a Cochrane review about vitamin E for neuroleptic-induced TD. It is not an RCT and does not test benzodiazepines.
This is an observational cohort study examining mortality rates in patients with schizophrenia and TD. It is not an RCT and does not test benzodiazepine treatment.
This is a Cochrane review about cholinergic drugs for TD. It is not an RCT and does not test benzodiazepines.
This is a Cochrane review about catecholaminergic drugs for TD. It is not an RCT and does not test benzodiazepines.
This RCT tests tetrabenazine for persistent phenothiazine dyskinesia, with diazepam as a control. The primary intervention is tetrabenazine, not a benzodiazepine.
Despite the title mentioning diazepam and TD, the abstract describes a preclinical study on graft versus host disease in rats examining Purkinje cell morphology. Not an RCT in humans.
This RCT primarily tests naltrexone (opioid antagonist) for TD treatment. While one arm includes clonazepam in combination, the primary intervention is naltrexone, not benzodiazepines.
This is a prospective naturalistic observational study comparing outcomes between patients with and without TD. It is not an RCT and does not test benzodiazepine treatment.
This is a review article discussing various therapeutic options for TD including clonazepam. It is not an RCT and does not present original trial data.
This is a 12-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized crossover trial testing clonazepam (benzodiazepine) in 19 chronically ill patients with tardive dyskinesia. Meets all criteria.

This study uses an ABA' research design to investigate diazepam (benzodiazepine) effects on TD in 21 patients. While not a traditional parallel-group RCT, it is a controlled experimental design testing benzodiazepine treatment for TD. Conservative approach favors inclusion.
This is a methodological paper about detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. It is not related to TD treatment or benzodiazepines.
This is a methodological paper about issues in meta-analysis of cluster randomized trials. It is not related to TD treatment or benzodiazepines.
This is a general review article about tardive dyskinesia covering prevalence, pathophysiology, and prevention. It is not an RCT and does not test benzodiazepine treatment.

This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques for cross-over trials. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD. The paper surveys Cochrane Library practices for synthesizing cross-over trial data.

This study tests benztropine and propranolol (not benzodiazepines) for tardive akathisia (not tardive dyskinesia). While it uses a random double-blind cross-over design, the intervention (benztropine/propranolol) and outcome (akathisia) do not match the review criteria.
This is a methodological paper about measuring inconsistency in meta-analyses. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.

This study tests diazepam (a benzodiazepine) for tardive dyskinesia. However, it uses an ABA design (single-subject design) rather than an RCT. The abstract states 'A rater-blind, ABA design study of 21 cases'. While this does not meet the RCT criterion, the study directly addresses benzodiazepines for TD and should be reviewed further to confirm study design details.

This is a methodological paper about variance components and intraclass correlations for survey design using Health Survey for England data. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.
This is a comparative before-and-after evaluation of CONSORT statement impact on RCT reporting quality. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.

This paper discusses TD incidence with atypical antipsychotics (olanzapine vs haloperidol). While it mentions a randomized study, the intervention being tested is antipsychotics (not benzodiazepines) and the outcome is TD incidence/prevention (not TD treatment). This does not match the review criteria.
This is a methodological paper about attrition issues in psychopharmacology RCTs. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.
This is a systematic review of methods for evaluating cluster-based interventions in health care. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.

This is a theoretical/review paper about the possible involvement of free radicals in neuroleptic-induced movement disorders. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.
This is a methodological paper about assessing quality of controlled clinical trials for systematic reviews. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.
This is a methodological paper about unit of analysis errors in studies of physicians' patient care behavior. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.
This is a methodological paper about imputing missing standard deviations in meta-analyses. It does not report an RCT testing benzodiazepines for antipsychotic-induced TD.

This is an observational 14-year follow-up study of TD and parkinsonism in psychiatric inpatients. It does not test benzodiazepines as an intervention and is not an RCT. The study assesses natural course of TD over time.
